utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. May we hear our case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian and Ruth Karper for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning. Anything to add before we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, an update on the constantly changing schedule and plans. The handwriting expert, as we mentioned before, the Court and counsel have had the English of that report since, I think, soon after the break. The translation is not yet -- the translation was provided yesterday, excuse me. The expert is prepared to testify tomorrow, to come and testify tomorrow. However, he requested to testify in the Dutch language. I've put in a request for that, and I haven't heard yet whether that's possible for tomorrow. They are checking on whether they can arrange that for tomorrow. Furthermore, although I'd also point out that I think Friday would be open because I spoke to Ms. Sutherland who is calling the witness on Thursday, and her estimate is that that would be a one-day witness. I've not yet had a chance to speak because he is not here, the person who wrote the report on the documents. And Ms. Tabeau's report, as I previously stated, she said would be ready by at least next Monday. However, I wanted to inform the Court and Defence counsel, I just spoke to them, that I would be willing on both the document report and Ms. Tabeau's updated report to submit those without the need for further examination, to submit the reports, if the Defence did not feel the need to cross-examine the witnesses. If they do, then I will call the witnesses; they will be available. That, I think, is the updates I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt preference should be given in case we need the expert witness on handwriting probably for a second time to at least start with his testimony, and everything should be done to make this possible. If a party needs assistance to come to this result, please, let us know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The one thing I did discuss with counsel, and perhaps Mr. Ostojic might address it, was I had mentioned earlier that I could use some time to speak to the witness and wouldn't mind starting a little later tomorrow. I actually am going to meet with the witness late this afternoon. But I don't think the witness is an all-day witness, so if we wanted to start at a later time, I think Mr. Ostojic had a reason why he would request that also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We should come back to this no later than quarter to 4.00 this afternoon when we know that it will be possible to provide the necessary translation into a language we all understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be fine. But I'm sure the translation unit would appreciate knowing the hours that the interpreter is needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We should be flexible. No doubt about this. May I ask about the witness on Thursday. You believe only one day. It will a crime-based witness. And what about protection? I wasn't quite clear on the basis of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: It's not a pure crime-based witness, as I recall. I'm not calling the witness, but I believe the witness did have, if I recall, some personal dealing with Dr. Stakic. But still, I think the witness has provided two statements that total five pages, so we don't expect it to be more than one day, the witness. Ms. Karper is checking on the protective measures. I believe that she is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What about the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Pseudonym. But in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Pseudonym, image, and voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. In principle, in open session. Would you be prepared to hear this witness, and what's your estimate? Can we manage it in one day?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning. If the OTP, Your Honour, takes a better part of the day, we would need at the very least one session, so that would be an hour and a half to two hours. We don't anticipate much longer from the estimate based on her statement. But I'd like, if I'm permitted to address another issue raised by the OTP, and respectfully to the Court, the scheduling we generally obviously don't mind when the Court advises they would like to defer the decision until a quarter to 4.00. It may become somewhat problematic to us because we would like to meet with Dr. Stakic at the Detention Unit tomorrow morning essentially to go over the handwriting expert's report among other reports. Now that we received it yesterday at the close of business or thereabouts. In order to schedule a meeting with Dr. Stakic at the Detention Unit, we would have to advise the authorities at Scheveningen at exactly what time and when. So to the extent the Court would give us at least some more latitude so that we could inform them and they could schedule the transportation back here for Dr. Stakic, we would appreciate that. But we also for other reasons, as stated by the OTP, would if possible like to start later tomorrow, either at 11.30 or at any time convenient for all the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So on the basis of the submissions of the parties, we should try to start at 11.00, that we have at least two entire sessions tomorrow. And I say now to whom it may concern, if it's possible to contact during this hearing the interpretation and translation unit to find out whether it's possible on this short notice to hear this witness speaking in Dutch from 11.00 until 4.00, with the ordinary one and a half hour break. So this should be scheduled for tomorrow. Is it enough to contact Dr. Stakic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So we only need the green light from the translation and interpretation unit, and I hope it will come out of the blue by fax or phone call. As regards our today's witness, the parties all have this enormous report. Any obstacles that we can start with this witness immediately?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask, then, the usher to bring in today's witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we start immediately by hearing your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's for you to start in French, Mr. Koumjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, would you please state your name for the record, and tell us your current employment.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: My name is Nicolas Sebire. I'm an investigator for the OTP at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Sebire, I know that you believe you speak some English. Please keep in mind that because of the interpretation, you have to wait until the answer is completely translated before -- the question, excuse me, is completely translated before giving your answer. Sir, how long have you worked for the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Since September 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what experience, if any, you had in law enforcement before joining the Office of the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I was a captain of the national police in France. I joined the national police in 1998. In 1999, I became part of the direction in Paris. I first served in the centre of the judicial police. In 1995, I joined the criminal brigade in Paris.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The criminal brigade in Paris, is it correct that that was a unit handling homicides? Can you tell us, what was the subject matter of the cases that you investigated in that division?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I was in a department which dealt mainly with political murders, assassinations, investigators into support groups, terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Since joining the Office of the Prosecutor, have you been assigned to Team 1 within the division of investigations?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In your work with Team 1, have you been working principally on one Prosecution, one case? And if so, which case was that?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: When I joined Team 1 in September 1999, I participated in an investigation into a case concerning Mr. Radislav Brdjanin and General Momir Talic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: As part of your responsibilities on that case, were you asked to do some work regarding individuals who had been exhumed or declared dead by courts in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, in fact, that's the case. I was in charge of a project which concerned exhumations in the northwestern region of Bosnia, as well as the analysis of declarations of death given to court municipalities in the Municipality of Kljuc and in the Municipality of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We'll come back and explain those declarations in more detail in a moment. Can you tell us the area of northwestern Bosnia that your work has covered in this project? Is that the area that was known in the period of 1992 as the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: How many different municipalities have you collected data for?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In the Autonomous Region of Krajina; it's composed of 25 municipalities. And as part of the investigation that we conducted, 16 municipalities were investigated. Up until now, the exhumations haven't taken place, haven't been carried out in all of these municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Going now to the actual project that you have been working on, would it be correct that there were two database aspects of your project, that you collected data from two separate sources of information? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And can you explain what those two different databases are?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The first database concerned exhumations, and in this database, we entered information concerning both the exhumations carried out by the Bosnian authorities, and the exhumations performed by the OTP. And in certain cases, exhumations which were jointly performed by the Bosnian authorities and the Tribunal. In the second database, there was information concerning declarations of death given by courts in Sanski Most and in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, have you written a report regarding your project entitled: "Additional Report, Exhumations and Proof of Death, Municipality of Prijedor"?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I don't recall the procedure we have been using on previous reports. Should the report now be marked as an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It will be marked as Exhibit S281.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Does the registry need another copy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any objections? I can't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then admitted into evidence, S281.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, before going into further explanations of your report, in reviewing your report, is it correct that you have some -- one or two corrections of information in the report?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Going to page 53 of the report, do you have it in front of you, sir? I see you do.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Referring to the second case listed in that report, that of Bego Salihovic, case number JK01281B, it indicates I believe that the person was -- I believe that each of these cases listed, according to what's stated on page 50, are people who were identified by DNA analysis. Was Bego Salihovic positively identified? In other words, were the remains that were found in that case number, case number 281B, positively identified as Bego Salihovic?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, they weren't. Bego Salihovic was not identified on the basis of DNA analysis. The results were negative in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that the DNA analysis showed that the remains were of someone from the family Salihovic, but could not be positively identified as Bego Salihovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, that's the case for another -- for the rest -- for the remains of another victim. And in fact, we know that he was part of a particular family, but up until now, we have not been able to determine which member of the family that person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So the case of Bego Salihovic, the remains in that case. 281B, were not identified through DNA. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Sir, going back to the two databases that you used, the exhumations, can you tell us how you obtained information regarding exhumations? What were the sources of information that you used in order to compile the data that you use in your report?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In the course of the previous years, the OTP has received from the Bosnian authorities reports concerning exhumations which were performed in the northwest of Bosnia. In general, these documents comprise reports established by the investigating judge in charge of the exhumations. They were accompanied by post mortem reports, identification reports, photograph albums made by scene of crime technicians in Bosnia, as well as sketches which establish a plan of the exhumation site which was excavated. In addition, we received identification reports established by the Bosnian authorities. In the case of the Bosnian authorities, these are the documents that we received on the most part from them. And the other part of the exhumation concerned exhumations carried out by the OTP, and we also have reports from forensic officers and from anthropologists, photographs taken during the exhumation and during the forensic investigations. We have videotapes showing the state of the exhumation site on a daily basis. There were reports of DNA analysis when such analysis were made. And in certain cases, reports concerning expert reports or analysis of earth samples, which were made when the exhumations were conducted. In general, these were the documents that we received in the case of exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, when you talk about post mortem reports, is it correct that you obtained normally a report by a pathologist as to any possible information regarding the cause of death or other remarkable conditions of the remains of the persons -- of the persons exhumed?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Within the Municipality of Prijedor, do you know how many individual and mass gravesites were exhumed?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Up until now, in the database, we have entered 261 sites which concern mass and individual gravesites in which individuals, bodies, were found and which belonged or which may have belonged to the Municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Within those 261 gravesites, your report indicates that 1394 bodies and body parts were exhumed. Can you explain the difference between body and body parts, and what's the significance of these terms?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I could, but it's not a domain that I'm specialised in. It's not really my domain. In general, these anthropologists at the exhumation sites who decide whether body parts belong to -- compose one body or whether they only -- the partial remains of a body, sir, I could not really provide a different explanation of these two terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that when bodies are exhumed generally, and when we're talking about the exhumations in this case of Prijedor, that most of the remains have decomposed so much that bones or bones and teeth are all that remain?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. In most of the cases, the bodies are in a skeletal state. In certain cases when we are talking about mass graves, big mass graves, the bodies would be in the centre, and you could still find tissue on these bodies. But this was not the case...

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I believe we lost the interpretation after the words: "But this was not the case."

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, in fact. That's correct. I will just read the transcript, if I may. What I said was that the fact that you found tissue on certain bodies, this didn't happen in most of the cases. In general, we had to deal with skeletons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you explain, who actually conducts the exhumations? And if counsel allows me to lead a little bit, is it correct, Mr. Sebire, that there are separate exhumation commissions for each of the three national communities in Bosnia, the Serbian, Bosniak, and Croat communities?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Each group has its own commission for searching for missing persons. These commissions are responsible for localising graves with individuals belonging to their ethnic group. When these common or individual graves are found, the judicial authorities, whether they be Bosniak or from Republika Srpska, have to organise an exhumation and to compile the reports on the basis of these investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that most of the exhumations in Prijedor that are in your report were exhumations most or all, please let us know, were exhumations performed by the Bosnian commission -- Bosniak, Bosniak commission of the federation?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you also request, as part of your duties beyond the case of Dr. Stakic information regarding exhumations conducted by the Republika Srpska, by the Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Koumjian. Wouldn't it be helpful to work with these purposes already now with Annex 16? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Which should be marked especially Exhibit 281-1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would the usher please put Annex 16, 281-1, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, before we go to the map, can you tell us -- you told us that there were 261 mass and individual gravesites. The diagram that's before us, this obviously does not depict all of the graves. Is that correct, all of the gravesites?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you explain what is depicted on this diagram in Annex 16?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Annex 16 is a map of the Municipality of Prijedor. And on this map, the general zones have been indicated, zones were exhumations were performed. Different colours have been used, and this indicates which organisations carried out certain exhumations. Blue shows the exhumations performed by the Bosnian authorities. Red shows the exhumations by the OTP. Green indicates exhumations performed by the Bosnian authorities, but the forensic investigations were carried out by the OTP in this case. And yellow indicates the exhumation sites which were exhumed by the Croatian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: How were most of these gravesites located in your experience?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Two answers are possible. The first one concerns the gravesites which are individual ones or small gravesites. In most cases, these gravesites would be identified because people present in the villages or family members buried the victims themselves. And in these cases, they indicated the exact location to the Bosnian authorities. In the case of mass graves such as the Jakarina Kosa, Pasinac, Kevljani, human sources provided indications or gave information after carrying out investigations in the field which allowed us to carry out exhumations as a result of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, your report indicates on page 5, the second paragraph, that "581 individuals were identified out of the 1394 cases exhumed, 573 were Bosnian Muslims, 7 were Bosnian Croats, and one was a Bosnian Serb." Can you tell us how individuals were identified from the remains exhumed? What was the procedure and criteria used to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Once again, it's necessary to distinguish between mass graves, relatively small mass graves, and individual graves. In cases when people participated in the burial, they would indicate the location of the gravesites. And in general, they provided the Bosnian authorities with information on the identity of the victims who were buried. If they didn't know the identity, they would sometimes provide information according to which they said they knew the victims by sight, that these victims were Muslims from Bosnia, from such and such a village, and they proceeded with the burial. In the case of more -- of bigger gravesites, the discovery of identification papers on the body, recognition on the basis of the clothes, and DNA analysis, these all are means that are used in order to identify the victim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that analysis of the remains determined that 10.000 -- I'm reading now the fourth paragraph on page 5 -- 1.039 were male, 84 were female. And for 271 cases, it was not possible to determine the gender. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your report goes on to indicate that "819 of the 1394 cases examined suffered gunshot injuries, these wounds being mainly located to the head and chest. 267 to the head, 234 to the head and chest, and 187 to the chest." First, is that correct? And secondly, can you tell us how that was determined when the remains are simply skeletons in most cases?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In fact, these figures are correct. This information is based on results of the post mortems that were carried out after these exhumations had been performed. So they based themselves on the information in the post mortem reports, and then they mentioned the number of gunshot wounds, the number of gunshot wounds that could be found there in the bones because there was no more tissue. So it was impossible to determine whether there were any other wounds because there were no traces left in tissue of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So if a bullet had passed, for example, through the chest without hitting any of the ribs, through the heart, and out the back without hitting any ribs, the pathologist would not be able to see the bullet strike on the bones; it was not manifest itself in the remains that were exhumed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your report further indicates that in 996 of these 1394 cases, there were grounds to show that the victim died in the course of the year 1992, and that the remaining 398 cases, the time of death was not determined. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, isn't it true that some people have been exhumed in Prijedor in which we know or you received information that they had died in, let's say, 1994, 1995, 1993? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In those cases, have you excluded them from your database and from the information provided in your report?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: These individuals are in the database, but they were excluded from the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So the figures that you are quoting, for example, the 1394 cases, would exclude any remains that were determined to have died in a year other than 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. The 1394 number concerned people for whom information shows that they died in 1992, or persons about whom we have no information regarding the date of their death.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Would it be a fair statement to say that based upon all the information that you have of exhumations to date in Prijedor, that the vast majority came -- the vast majority of those in which there is a date that can be determined died in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You use a second database, according to your report, the proof of death database. And you've mentioned already that these are based on court rulings, and you mentioned the two places, Sanski Most and I believe Kljuc courts that are actually issuing these rulings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you explain how it is that the courts in Sanski Most and Kljuc issue -- which court has jurisdiction over cases in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: If I've understood your question correctly, I would answer as follows: Many families from Prijedor are living in Sanski Most and Kljuc today. And for that reason, they turned to the municipal courts of those towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly the procedure that family members would go through in order to have a relative declared to be dead by one of these courts?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I don't know the procedure -- that is, all the details of the procedure. But what I do know is that a missing person or a person who has been missing for several years, there is then a member of his family which can go to the Court where he lived and make a request for that person to be declared dead officially. Apparently, this procedure requires that witnesses come to indicate when the person was last seen or what the date was or the time was that the person died. On the basis of that testimony, there is a judicial decision taken declaring the person officially dead. Ordinarily, the decision also indicates the date which is considered the date of death.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with any procedure following the testimony of the family members for some publication to be made of the person's name, person who is missing?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I think that after the judgement is rendered, it's published, and after a certain amount of time, I can't tell you what it is unfortunately, when the person's officially declared dead because there was no response to the call or in any case that no -- we did not -- or that people would -- nobody would appear to say that the person who was officially declared dead in fact was still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that from this database of missing persons -- excuse me, persons declared dead what you've labelled the proof of death database that you had information at the time of writing this report regarding 1.295 court rulings declaring individuals from Prijedor as officially dead, and that in 955 of these cases, it's indicated by the ruling that the person was killed or went missing in the course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, but it's 955 cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Of these cases, 49 were female; 7 were under 16; and 72 were over the age of 60. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the figures that we just mentioned solely concerned the Municipality of Prijedor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Going now just to page 7 of your report, paragraph labelled 3.2, is it correct that from these courts you've received a total of 2.026 court rulings regarding eight separate municipalities of the former Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So from these eight municipalities, well over half, 1295, came from Prijedor alone. Is that correct? Almost two thirds.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that represents a little bit more than 60 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, you have a couple of charts in your report on page 14. And Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I've asked you to bring, I believe you have with you, figure 1 and figure 2 to put on the ELMO. Is that correct, you have those, or have you given them to Ms. Karper? This is on page 14, but if there are extra copies, if we could have one for each of the Judges. If there is still another one -- we have the report. I'm sorry, Mr. Sebire, how many copies did you make of that?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I think about ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Then perhaps one could be given to each of the Defence attorneys and to each of the Judges, and if I could have one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And perhaps one to the registry. Perhaps we should mark this as a separate exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would be S281-2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In the explanation for this diagram, figure 1, actually appears on the bottom of page 13 of your report. Is it correct, Mr. Sebire, that this diagram, figure 1, depicts graphically the total number of persons exhumed, and then breaks it down by the female and male population, and also indicates for each of these populations the age, whether the individual was below 16, over 60, or within the ages of 16 to 60. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. We're talking about nonexhumed persons, dead people, those who were declared dead by the municipal courts and were not exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. So you're dealing here with declarations of death by the courts. And to be clear, on your criteria, below 16 means age 15 and below, and over 60 means age 61 and above. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct, then, that a total of 49 females were exhumed, two below 15 -- 15 or below, and seven 61 or above?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That of the males exhumed, five were 15 and below, and sixty-five were 61 or above?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You have a second diagram, figure 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: May that be distributed now, please. Your Honour, would this be marked -- would it be 281-3?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Again, this diagram is dealing with the Court declarations of death. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And in figure 2, S281-3, you've indicated for each of the declarations of death in which a month or date is indicated when the person disappeared or was killed, you've categorised all of those declarations according to the month that the person disappeared or was killed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it clear, then, that this diagram should total and does total 955 separate declarations of death and that of these 955 declarations of death, 952 of these cases occurred between April and September 1992?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, in the exhumations, did you personally visit any of the sites where exhumations took place?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. I was involved in the exhumation in Redak, in the Ljubija mine area in Prijedor. That was an exhumation which took place in June of 2000. I was also involved in the exhumation --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry. Perhaps if we could have the Annex 16 put back on the ELMO. As you speak of each of these sites, if you could identify them on the Annex 16, S281-1.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As I was saying, I was involved in the exhumation in Redak, which you can see here. The one who was in Jakarina Kosa. There are two exhumation sites which are in the mining zone of Ljubija. In Prijedor -- those are the two I was involved in, the two only ones. And I also went to exhumation sites that had been exhumed in the past in order just to go on site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you indicate where those are.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In the Hambarine region, Biscani, Kozarac, Kamicani. Those are the major areas where I went.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The site you indicated as Redak, is it correct that that is by the Ljubija mines?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: As part of your work on this case, did you attempt to provide the Court with information regarding links between specific killings charged in the indictment against Dr. Stakic, the 20 specific killings, and exhumations of remains or court declarations of death of individuals?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. That's in the third part of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you explain how you went about establishing the links.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The primary information source was the use of the witness statements who had been called to testify in this trial to verify in respect of the victims' names mentioned whether those persons had been declared dead by a court or whether those persons had been exhumed and identified in Prijedor or in neighbouring municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So I want to go through some of this with you. And we begin with the exhumations regarding killings charged in paragraph 44 of the indictment, those not connected to detention facilities. Is it correct -- and we're talking now about Kozarac. Can you just comment, Mr. Sebire, upon exhumations performed in the vicinity of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. In general, there were about -- there were about 104 exhumations that were performed in common or individual graves during which 188 bodies were exhumed. When we went to -- spoke with the various witnesses called in this trial, we were able to verify that some of the victims mentioned had been exhumed, in particular, the exhumation which took place in Sivci Mihtov on the 21st of October, 1998, by the Bosnian authorities. That was the date a mass grave was exhumed by the Bosnian authorities. And there was also -- there was an individual grave with the body of a Javor Radocaj who was mentioned as well by the witnesses. That body was exhumed and identified. In other cases, witnesses gave the names of victims for whom we still have not exhumed the body, or at least whose body has not been identified. But for whom there are declarations of death saying that the person was, in fact, killed in the Kozarac area during May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that of the 20 killings charged in the indictment in which you attempted to provide links, you found no links, in other words, no persons exhumed and identified, nor a court ruling of a declaration of death of a person mentioned by a witness, for two of those, Hambarine and Brisevo?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that, just to go over those, first tell us about Brisevo. Did you receive information regarding exhumations conducted in that area?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Who conducted those exhumations?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was the Croatian branch of the federal commission for missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Have you received any information from that commission for your databases?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, not to date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And is it correct for Hambarine that although no individuals were exhumed, you state on page 18 that 31 individuals were exhumed from 15 mass and individual graves? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: 27 of these individuals, the post mortem determined that the cause of death was from gunshot injuries? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Before we go on, when we talk about -- you said you linked witness statements or witness reports to exhumations and proof of deaths, what group of persons did you select regarding the witnesses? Did you select all statements from Prijedor in the possession of the OTP; and if not, why not?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: You're talking about the testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry. You said in order to link -- to provide the links that are in this third part of your report, you looked at your exhumation and proof of death databases and compared those to the reports of witnesses as to persons who had been killed or disappeared. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And is it correct that you were actually given specific instructions to only use the statements of witnesses who have testified live or 92 bis in the Stakic trial?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So you did not use all witness statements from witnesses from Prijedor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just tell the Court, do you know approximately how many witness statements there are from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Well, it would be difficult to give an exact figure. But as far as I know, about 1.500 statements either taken by the Office of the Prosecutor or interviews that were given to us by the Bosnian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't want to go over each of these because the Judges have your report, and they can read the report itself. But I want to highlight a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. few of these. Let's go to page 19 of your report regarding links between the killings in Biscani on or about the 20th of July. Can you tell us how many bodies from how many graves were exhumed in Biscani?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As of today, 82 bodies were exhumed from 22 mass and individual gravesites.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us how these individuals -- what information you obtained regarding -- from the post mortem examinations of the remains as to the -- let me try that question again. Can you tell us from the information you obtained regarding the post mortem autopsies of the remains any information regarding the cause of death of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In 64 cases, the cause of death was determined as having resulted from gunshot injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And is it correct that these figures do not include information from Jakarina Kosa, that mass grave? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We'll go into a little bit more detail on that exhumation. But briefly, can you tell us now where did that -- what time did the exhumation take place in Jakarina Kosa, during what year and month?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The exhumation took -- well, began on the 11th of September last year. And it lasted five weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you show us on the diagram where -- again where Jakarina Kosa is.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to go to page 26 of your report in which you discuss links regarding the killing of a number of men in the Ljubija iron ore mine on or about the 25th of July. Can you tell us what exhumations took place in the area of the Ljubija mine and the Ljubija football stadium?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: There was an -- one exhumation in Redak. That was one that was performed fully by the OTP. Redak is right here. Talking about distances, it must be about 5 or 6 kilometres from the town of Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. So just to give an example of the exercise you did with the links, let's take the witness listed as P38 - I'm not going to state the name in Court - on page 27 of your report. In the third paragraph under his name you say: "Amongst those killed on that day, the witness recalls, and you list several names. Among those names are Islam Hopovac.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Also someone named Kadiric, someone named Kekic, and someone named Kadic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that from the exhumations that were performed, that some identification was done or made regarding, for example, Islam Hopovac?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. His body was identified in the Redak mass grave exhumation site. It was discovered and registered as RK01203A.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it also correct that for the --

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: B rather, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it also correct that in these exhumations, identification documents were found - we're now going to footnote 62, 63, and 64 of your report - for someone bearing the name Kadiric, Hilmija; three identification documents with the family named Kekic; and three identification documents bearing the family name Kadic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. During the exhumation, identification documents of the name Hilmija was found. Identification documents with Kekic as a family name, Kekic, Nurudin; Kekic, Esad; and Kekic, Asmir, as well as identification documents with the Kadic family name, that is Kadic, Armin; Kadic, Edin; and Kadic, Vahidin. All names which were mentioned by Witness P38.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The next witness I will mention by name because he testified in open session. Did you receive information from Nermin Karagic?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In fact, did you speak to Nermin Karagic near the site of the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that one of the bodies that was exhumed was identified through DNA analysis was exhumed from Redak as the father of Nermin Karagic?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That the autopsy report concluded that Ferid Karagic, the father, died of gunshot injuries to the head and chest?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did Nermin Karagic also describe some other individuals that he saw at the execution sites that day, and do you recall one description in particular?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. The first time that I met that witness, he went to the exhumation site for which he didn't have access for reasons of preserving things and for security reasons. We agreed that we would meet again after the work day was over, and he gave me information of names that he remembered having been there in the bus, and he specifically mentioned the person of Ekrem Duratovic, telling me that that person, as far as he remembered, was wearing -- the last time he saw him in the bus, he was wearing blue work clothes. And he stated in detail that the -- that there were buttons on the jacket, that is, blue plastic buttons on the jacket. About three days later during the exhumation, there was a body found which had been skeletonised. There were remains of a blue work jacket with blue buttons, was discovered. In one of the pants' pockets, which was in very good shape, we found an identity document bearing his name, Ekrem Duratovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The same name that had been given to you by Mr. Nermin Karagic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: From the autopsies performed of the remains exhumed from Redak, did you make some -- compile some figures on page 28 of your report regarding the cause of death that was determined when it could be determined, and is it correct that 37 of these cases involved multiple gunshot injuries?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. In 37 cases, it was determined that the victims had multiple gunshot injuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You indicated that 64 bodies and 28 body parts were examined, and that -- is it correct that the pathologist found evidence, and correct me if I am wrong, I presume evidence from bones that have been hit, that 304 shots had been fired and struck the victims? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of the examination conducted on the remains of the bodies exhumed from this site, a total of 304 gunshot wounds were found. Traces of these wounds were found in the bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move on now to killings in -- excuse me, before I move on, two of the specific killings charged in the indictment, one involves, not in a detention facility, was the 21st of August at Vlasic mountain. To your knowledge, have any bodies been exhumed from those persons executed on the 21st of August at Vlasic mountain?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Another killing charged in a detention facility is the Room 3 massacre at Keraterm. To your knowledge, have any bodies been exhumed and identified from the Room 3 massacre at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Not as far as I know, but it's necessary to take into consideration the number of bodies that were exhumed and haven't been identified to date. It's possible that they have been exhumed; but to date, no kind of formal identification allows us to make such a claim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that very many bodies have been exhumed; but because of the state of being principally skeletons, no identification has been made? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: On page 31 of your report -- excuse me. Let's go back to page 30. However, from the Keraterm camp, can you tell us if any bodies have been exhumed and identified, or if court declarations of death have been sent to you regarding individuals killed in the Keraterm camp? Let's take those separately; first, the court declarations of death.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. We received 64 declarations of death concerning individuals who were seen for the last time or who were killed in Keraterm in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, going to bodies exhumed, can you please discuss whether any individuals were exhumed that were identified as being from the Keraterm camp, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Once more, through the witness who was called to the present trial and who mentioned victims, some of them were, in fact, exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And you're referring to the witness identified on page 30 of your report as P50. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite correct. He specifically mentions two individuals who were exhumed at the exhumation site called Pasinac. This exhumation was performed by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I want to ask you specifically about a person exhumed, Jovan Radocaj. Was a body exhumed and identified by that name from the Pasinac cemetery?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. But it's a separate exhumation which was conducted by the Bosnian Commission for Missing Persons. We haven't received all the documents concerning this exhumation, but this individual was, in fact, exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnicity of that individual?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As far as I know, that individual was of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In your report, you indicate that this Jovo or Jovan was a member Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of the SDA. Where did you obtain that information?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This information was obtained when interviewing Witness P50.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, moving on to page 31, this Court has heard testimony beginning, in fact, with Witness B and also Witness A. From Witness B, that on the 5th of August of 1992, two buses left the Keraterm camp. After men were selected, names were read out, two buses left that camp, and those individuals have not been seen. And also from Witness A that certain individuals, that those buses went to Omarska where certain other individuals were put on buses and they have not been seen. Did you determine whether any bodies have been exhumed from individuals who have been named by witnesses to have been on these buses that left the Keraterm camp and stopped in the Omarska camp on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. The Bosnian authorities exhumed a mass grave called Hrastova Glavica; it's a cave. 126 bodies were found in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. Can you indicate on the map where that mass gravesite is located.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: It's not on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. It's in Sanski Most. Correct? Okay. I'm sorry. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Of the 126 bodies that were exhumed at Hrastova Glavica, the Bosnian authorities determined that two bodies were individuals who had been in the cave for many years. One of the individuals was apparently a victim of someone who was killed in the Second World War. As far as the 124 other bodies, we have identified a certain number of them by the Bosnian authorities, 47 of them so far. And given the testimony of people who have been here, there was a connection which was established between the presence of these individuals in the buses that left Keraterm and went to Omarska, and then disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You didn't -- I said it, but you didn't actually state it. Where was this mass gravesite located, in what municipality?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: This mass gravesite is in the municipality of Sanski Most, which is south of the Municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you give us an estimate of the distance from the town of Prijedor to Hrastova Glavica.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Probably between 30 and 35 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us, of the 124 bodies recovered whether the post mortems were able to determine the cause of death in any of cases? And by 124, I'm excluding the two bodies that apparently came from World War II.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. In 121 of the cases, the forensic experts determined that the cause of death was gunshot wounds. And for the 47 individuals who were identified in the course of this exhumation, the cause of death is the same, gunshot wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Of the three remaining cases, were the pathologists able to give an opinion as to the cause of death of any of these three remaining cases?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. In one case, the cause of death was a wound caused by an explosive device, a hand grenade or something like that. And in two other cases, the cause of death was the result of wounds inflicted by a blunt instrument.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: On those bodies where the cause of death was determined to be gunshot injury, was there evidence of other blunt-trauma injuries?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In the report, it says that -- the report mentions the main cause of death. Nevertheless, forensic investigations show that most bodies also show signs of wounds inflicted by blunt instruments, so signs of blunt trauma.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. I'm sorry to interrupt this witness statement, but I learned that there are, indeed, some problems to get at least two interpreters from Dutch to English. The responsible section of this Tribunal will try the very best to have another person. One would be available, but it could be of assistance if the witness would be prepared to testify in English with the assistance of one person doing the interpretation in the courtroom. That means that when the interpreter would be present here in the courtroom, and if the witness needs some assistance, then he could get this by a professional interpreter. This would be the one available solution. If you could be so kind, Mr. Koumjian, and contact the witness whether or not he's prepared to do it this way. But nevertheless, until the break, the section will try to find a second interpreter. Now we can proceed with the hearing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, I want to direct your attention to page 34 of your report and ask you now regarding your project to establish links regarding killings of men in the Omarska camp between late May and the 6th of August, 1992. Can you tell us from the Omarska camp whether individuals who were detained there have been exhumed; and if so, from how many different gravesites?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Persons who were seen in Omarska for the last time and who were killed there were exhumed, both by the Bosnian authorities and by the OTP. To date, there have been five mass gravesites. They are mentioned in the report. The first one is Kozarusa Patrija 4, then we have Kevljani, Jama Lisac, Hrastova Glavica, and Jakarina Kosa.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In addition to individuals exhumed from Omarska, did you obtain information regarding individuals last seen in that camp who have been declared dead by the courts of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, this concerns 145 individuals. We received declarations from municipal courts indicating that 145 individuals were killed or seen for the last time in the Omarska camp between the 28th of May and the 6th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I want to skip ahead for a moment and talk about the Trnopolje camp. Have any individuals, to your knowledge, been exhumed and identified who were last seen in the Trnopolje camp or went missing from there or were known to have been killed at the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As far as I know, there haven't been any exhumations of individuals from the Omarska camp -- the Trnopolje camp. Correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct -- let me now ask you, how many individuals last seen at that camp have been declared dead by the courts of Bosnia, according to the information you have received?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: To date, we have received 28 declarations of this kind for persons who were seen for the last time or who were killed in Trnopolje according to witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it also correct that from the witness statements, you were not able to make a link between those witness statements of persons missing and those 28 declarations of death?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I want to go back now and talk to you a bit about some of the mass gravesites, starting on page 38 of your report, with Kevljani. This is a grave in the municipality of Prijedor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Were you present during the exhumation at Kevljani?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many bodies were recovered from that site.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: 72 bodies were exhumed from 15 different graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You've used that word "grave" and we've used the word "gravesite." Can you tell us what is the definition you're using for a grave. So Kevljani itself is a gravesite, is that correct, and you said 15 individual graves. What is the definition of a "grave"?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: There's a difference between a mass grave and an individual grave. You want me to make this distinction. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. Is it correct that the archeologists actually determine how many graves are at a location?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that in one gravesite it can contain multiple graves. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the case in Kevljani, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And one grave can contain either one body or multiple bodies. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And I'm asking you this - I do not know the answer, but if you do, please let us know - is then the definition of a grave basically a hole dug in the ground, and that when we say 15 individual graves at Kevljani, we mean that the archeologists determined that there were 15 separate holes dug in which bodies were dumped at that gravesite?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Five individual graves in which bodies were found. If I use the term "mass grave," this is because these bodies weren't buried, let's say, in an appropriate way, in a way one would imagine in a normal burial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: By the way, is there something distinctive about how the practice -- the cultural practice of Bosnian Muslims in how they bury their dead that would allow you to make a determination from the manner in which the grave appears whether it was a burial done by Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, there is an indication when an exhumation is performed. It's the position of the body in the grave. If it is -- if the head is pointing towards Mecca, then one may think that someone buried the body by -- that the body was buried by someone of the same faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Are there any other distinctive ways in which the graves are constructed in the cultural practice of Bosnian Muslims in your experience?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Once the body has been placed at the bottom of the tomb, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. it's usually wrapped in a sheet and there are wood planks which are installed in the tomb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So in other words not a casket, but the wooden planks are above the body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: At Kevljani, was there evidence that that site had been disturbed, and can you explain your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I apologise. Part of the sites which were discovered by the archeologist -- well, their contents had been robbed, about 73 partial bodies were discovered in the pit, in pits that had been robbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When you say the pits had been robbed, do you mean someone simply removed jewellery or valuables that might have been buried with the bodies, or that the actual remains of the deceased had been removed?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: When I talk about graves that had been robbed, these are graves from which the bodies that had been buried were taken. Certain elements, certain remains allowed archeologists to determine more or less the number of individuals who should have been present in these graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct, looking at page 38 of your report, that the archeologist determined that there had been 26 graves, and that several of them, for example, graves 1, 3, and 26, had been completely robbed, and others robbed to the base, and these are listed? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You've indicated in your report that 73 -- excuse me, 72 complete bodies were found, and that approximately 70 body parts were found. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And that of these bodies, is it correct that a relatively small percentage showed evidence of gunshot injuries, that according to page 39 of your report, there were 11 gunshot injuries on those bodies, according to the report of Dr. John Clark?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: However, there was a lot of evidence of blunt-force trauma, and in fact in 86 per cent of the 73 bodies, there was evidence of blunt-force trauma to the ribs in addition to various percentages given for other parts of the body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that of these individuals exhumed, that there were 12 identifications, 7 by DNA, and you list Those individual identifications in your report, and that these individuals came from a variety of locations, Stara Rijeka, Kozarac, Kozarusa, Ljubija? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Of those 12 identifications, 3 were of Croat ethnicity, and the remainders were Bosniaks or Bosnian Muslims. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct also.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to Jama Lisac gravesite. Can you correct my pronunciation and tell us where that gravesite is located.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Jama Lisac is in the municipality of Krupa Na Uni.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that Krupa Na Uni is a post-Dayton municipality, or it was created after the Dayton accords, and that it lies, I believe, is it correct, to the northwest of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. The site itself is right to the west of Prijedor, almost on the border between the two municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us what you found or what was found at the Krupa Na Uni exhumation in Jama Lisac?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: It was an exhumation which was performed by the Bosnian authorities for -- on whom forensic tests were carried out by the OTP's forensic team. 55 bodies, and 1 body part were found during that exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And can you explain what that site looks like? Were the bodies buried in the earth?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I didn't go to the site itself, but apparently it was a cave. And the bodies were found piled on top of one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that the archeologist determined that the minimum number of bodies represented by the remains found was 51 individuals?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. That is what the pathologist's report established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Of those 51 minimum number of bodies, 46 were determined to have died from gunshot injury, 2 from blunt-force trauma, and 3 the cause of death was undetermined?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Do you know, of those persons identified, can you tell us how many were identified and where those individuals came from?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In all six individuals identified on that site, there were four men and two women who were identified. As regards the two women, identification was done through a DNA analysis. And apparently, they turned out to be -- both of them were detainees from the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that those two women were Edna Dautovic and Sureta Medunjanin, the wife of Becir Medunjanin, and the mother of Adis Medunjanin?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that among the others, identification was -- other persons identified were Ekrem Alic who was seen in the Omarska camp, and Smail Alic who was also seen in the Omarska camp until taken away by a bus in late August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that exhumations were also done in a cemetery which is a place perhaps where we would expect to find deceased persons, Pasinac in Prijedor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. In the Pasinac cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Some of the persons exhumed had been mentioned in the statement of Witness 50 who testified in this case. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Among -- your report indicates on page 45 that 45 bodies and 3 body parts were recovered, which included 9 females, and 3 bodies for which no gender was determined. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. The report says that 44 men, 9 women, and 3 individuals whose gender could not be determined. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And two of the bodies exhumed, were those children?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The pathologist's report indicates that for 26 of these bodies, the cause of death was determined to be gunshot injury. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And that in one of these cases, the cause of death was determined to be strangulation by ligature. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Two other bodies, the cause of death was blunt-force trauma, and in 27 bodies, the cause of death could not be ascertained. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's also correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct that some of these bodies -- well, specifically in case PC -- on page 46 of your report, the case of the body identified as Safet Mesic, that according to a witness that this person had been in the Keraterm camp and had died in the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, we have a decision declaring that person deceased. In the decision, it states that a witness testified and indicated that the victim was a detainee at the Keraterm camp where he was beaten and died from the consequences of the mistreatment that he was a victim of.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: There's also an identification on page 47 of your report of Emsud Bahonic, and is it correct the court ruling indicates that this victim died in the Keraterm camp after being tortured?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I want to move on to the exhumation at Jakarina Kosa. Did you attend this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, can you tell us for how long you were present during this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I was there for five weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you describe the location of Jakarina Kosa and the place where the bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The Jakarina Kosa site is in the mining area of Ljubija between the town of Ljubija and Stari Majdan. The site itself is in an open mine which one could say is no longer being used. Part of the terracing used previously for mining had disappeared, and had been replaced by a slope about 85 metres long. During the searches that were made in that slope, we found bodies. All in all, about 373 were found during that exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When you say 373 bodies, is it correct that as the site is being dug, bodies or bones were found when the bones were believed initially to belong to one person, they were put into one body bag, and that's how you ended up with 373 body bags? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: More or less. If you allow me to give you some details on that subject, the exhumation itself was you could say rather difficult because we were working on a slope. The climate, the weather conditions also deteriorated, made the work harder. On several occasions the slope collapsed on the areas that had been uncovered during the exhumations. Even though there was an anthropologist on site, it was difficult onsite to determine exactly what parts of a body fit with another body part. This study was done subsequently during the forensic operations. And the anthropologists from the OTP were able to determine that out of all of the human remains taken from that mass grave we were dealing with a minimum of about 288 individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, can you explain the difference in the terminology, the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. two terms, "primary" and "secondary" gravesite?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Very briefly, a primary site is one for which there is no proof that -- there was an attempt to change the site, that there was no attempt of theft made or attempts made to move the bodies within the site. A secondary site would have the bodies that were stolen or removed from a site.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So a secondary site would be a location where the bodies were not initially buried, but were moved to following their initial burial. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. A secondary site is not the place where the body was initially buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was there evidence that you obtained as to when the bodies were placed in the Jakarina Kosa gravesite?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: There is a witness, P53, who described how in June, July 1993, there was vehicle movement moving toward Jakarina Kosa which describes that the area was closed to everybody for a certain amount of time. There was a dreadful stench in that region. The sounds of mechanical -- mechanical sounds that were being made, and the witness thought that they were tools used in order to dig holes in mines. And then afterwards, he heard explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is it correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, may I just interrupt for one moment. I want to follow the testimony in a better way. You speak sometimes about Witness 50 or P50. Could it be --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I could tell you. That's Witness O in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Do we have any charts indicating who is Witness 50 or 53 or whatever?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness 50 is a witness who testified in this trial as Witness O under that pseudonym. Witness 53 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We have a number of witnesses called now P50, P53, and so on. Where can we find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The numbers that Mr. Sebire is using are the 65 ter numbers. And Witness 50, as I mentioned, is Witness O who has testified. Witness 53 is a 92 bis number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 65 ter number, this is the basis. No additional numeration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And Witness 53, just for the record, Witness N, a 92 bis witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, the area that Witness N or Witness 53 was speaking about, did he indicate who controlled that area at the time that he heard the explosions and you said the area was blocked off?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.
