utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was the area controlled at that time by the VRS, by the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, or at least that's what the witness states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In the site itself, in the exhumation, did you -- can you tell us if you found any evidence of military presence or involvement in the burial?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Between the 18th and 21st of September, 2001, five parts of an unidentified substance were discovered at that point. The analysis which was done later showed that they were military explosives, Pentrite-type explosives. In addition, what was also discovered was a rather large number of military gas masks, gas cartridges, and plastic gloves, green ones, which I would call military green or olive-drab.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was a helmet also discovered?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned that the Witness 53 discussed his observations in 1995, and it appeared the bodies were buried at that time. The bodies that were exhumed, were any of them identified?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Some of them were identified. The period that the witness was talking about was 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you. Can you tell us, of those persons identified, I believe is it correct that there were 12 identifications to date?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: 11 positive identifications using DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And for how many of those 11 was it determined that the person was last seen in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Seven cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And is it correct that in the other four cases, there is no date indicated? There's no determination as to when the person died or went missing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: To date, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, you've talked about the data that you do have available. First of all, do you have any reason to believe that all bodies buried in Prijedor have been discovered and exhumed?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I don't think so myself, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In fact, you've already indicated that for probably the two largest killings in our indictment, Room 3 and Vlasic mountain, no bodies have been exhumed and identified. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Regarding the Court declarations of death you briefly described the procedures. Is it correct that the number of reports that you have of persons missing, you only get a report of a person missing and declared dead if family members go to the Court and request such a ruling and comply with the various requirements of the law in Bosnia to get a declaration of death? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If the family is not interested in getting a declaration of death for whatever reason, or if no family members survive, there would be no declaration of death. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Finally, on the sites, have you often dealt with family members of those exhumed?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Ordinarily, when an exhumation is performed, it is not infrequent that people show up on site thinking that some of the members of their families might be in the site being exhumed. And so it is not unusual to run into family members at the exhumation sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In your experience in dealing with these family members, does it appear to you that the people from Bosnia, that in their culture, it is important to find the graves of family members who have been killed and that they have lost during years as far back as 1992?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we proceed immediately with the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, my name is John Ostojic, and along with Branko Lukic, we represent Dr. Milomir Stakic. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me by way of your background -- I know that you're involved or were involved previously in law enforcement. Can you tell me where is it that you learned English?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In France.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the report that we have that's been identified titled "Exhumations and Proof of Death, Municipality of Prijedor" was that compiled by you yourself, sir?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: A couple of questions in connection with the introductory remarks in your report, if I may just for purposes of clarification for myself. You mention several times, at least I count four, but in the introduction you mention on a number of occasions the issue of risk of double counting. Can you please explain to me what that means.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the main reasons why we use two different databases, one for the exhumations; the other for those persons declared dead -- deceased. As you saw, many -- several bodies were exhumed and up to date have not yet been identified, and it may be that the nonidentified bodies be people -- are people who were declared dead by a court. But When you add up both figures of people deceased and people declared deceased and those who were exhumed, there is a risk of double counting some of them. And that is why it seemed better.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for me what the level of risk is even by separating the two databases and providing the analysis that you did? Would the risk be high, moderate, or low for purposes of double counting individuals or bodies that were recovered?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't believe that question can be answered. He said that they were separated, and the question is, as I understand it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It may be the witness has some founded estimate on this question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The risk could be that either all the bodies which were exhumed and not identified were not declared deceased either, and that you would add up both figures and you would give you a number that would be the result of adding up the two assumptions, or that all of the people exhumed and were not identified were also declared deceased. And in those cases, they have got to be subtracted so that one can have a total figure. It is difficult to quantify double counting risks when one is dealing with nonidentified bodies to date. In order to avoid that risk, that's why we decided to count them separately so that they should not be -- make any attempt at adding or subtracting. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: This is an eerie kind of area for me. With respect to the different kind of body parts that were exhumed, did you examine whether there was a risk of double counting those that were exhumed by the OTP, those that were exhumed by the OTP in assistance and cooperation with the Bosnian authorities, and those that were exhumed by the Bosnian authorities individually of the 261 gravesites that were exhumed?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The risk of double counting does not have to do with those individuals who were exhumed. The risk is if you try to get a total figure by adding the persons declared deceased and the persons exhumed. The problem of the number of bodies and body parts is not the same thing. That relates only to the exhumations. And in this case, it was no problem -- there was no risk of double counting here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in your opinion, there was a low, if any, risk of double counting based on your analysis. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: My objection is the question is vague as to double counting what? I don't think if the witness answers we would know what the answer --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may reply, Your Honour, the witness in the last sentence in his answer on page 49, line 8 clearly states: "There was no risk of double counting here." So I think at the very least, I should have an opportunity to clarify that and to determine whether or not the level of risk that he believes was either low, moderate, or high, or nonexistent. And all I'm doing is following up on the answer that the witness gave on line 8 of that page. It's not that major of a point, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: My understanding of the original question, as I understood it, was the risk of double counting as the witness explained of exhumations and the court declarations. Because the witness has explained that no attempt was made to add those two figures, then it's not relevant what the risk was because it could not occur because they were not added together. He has explained that you cannot add the exhumations and the Court declarations together without possibly double counting some individuals. And that's why he has not done it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we ask the witness to comment on this interesting discussion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So once more, in order to avoid any problems, in order to avoid double counting, we didn't add the number of persons deceased, the number of persons declared deceased by municipal courts to the total number of bodies or of body parts that were exhumed. The reason for this was that there was a large number of bodies or body parts that were not identified. Now, it seems to me that Mr. Ostojic was asking a question with regard to the exhumations carried out by the Bosnian authorities and those carried out by the OTP, that I'm not sure that I have understood his question very well given that a body or a body part is only counted once. So I don't see how double counting could be a problem, how you could double count a body or a body part because they are exhumed only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you've answered my question, but if I may proceed, Your Honour, is it fair to state that there was no reliance placed on this book that you cite on page 15 under footnote number 14 "Ni Krivi Ni Duzni" because, essentially, of the reasons that you've just outlined for us, namely, there would be a risk of double counting and, in fact, if you make a comparative analysis of that book, the claims offered by the OTP and your tables, it would be almost impossible not to conclude, sir, that double counting and the risk of double counting would be extremely high?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The book in question refers to persons who were missing. I used it in certain cases in order to obtain information with regard to the probable date when the person went missing. This book includes persons who were exhumed, as well as persons who were declared deceased. And obviously, also a number of persons who were neither exhumed nor declared deceased but who are still missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please be kind enough to translate the name of this book on footnote 14, page 15, "Ni Crivi Ni Duzni," Knjiga nestalij opcine Prijedor, into English and French. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Not Guilty. The Book of Missing Persons in the Municipality of Prijedor."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to interrupt Mr. Ostojic's examination - I leave it up to him - but I realise now that I meant to introduce this book during Mr. Sebire's testimony and briefly comment on the update that we are expecting, or have him comment on that. But whenever Your Honour feels that's appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Does the Defence allow this interruption of the cross-examination by handing out this book? Probably it's easier for you to make reference on this basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's acceptable, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise for not doing it sooner. May the book --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any objections against the admission into evidence as S282?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do, Your Honour, have an objection. We have an objection essentially that the book is not something that is widely acceptable - hopefully we'll get that information from the witness - that has not been relied on by the witness. By the witness's very own testimony before us, Mr. Sebire, he states that in order to avoid the risk of double counting, that only specific sources were used; namely, two: The exhumations and the certificates of death or, as I think identified in his report, proof of death. I think that it's not only cumulative for purposes of our discussions, but also inappropriate respectfully to allow a book of an author who can summarise and tell us what his opinion based on, perhaps, incomplete information when certain individuals were missing or were presumed dead. I think Mr. Sebire's report respectfully, and without prejudice to us, does a fairly adequate job and is rather impressive to identify that 581 specific individuals have been named and identified of the 1.294 [sic] or so that have been exhumed. It is from that basis we believe that there may be some proof of death, but utilising that book would be outside the scope and scheme of the rules prescribed by the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So this document is now only provisionally marked as S282. We leave the admission into evidence open. I think we will hear something during the cross-examination about the pros and cons of this book. But may it please be distributed by the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I perhaps could get from Mr. Sebire or just represent to the Court that this book was compiled some years ago. It's dated April 2000. And that Mr. Sebire has asked for and hopefully should obtain in the next week or so an electronic version of an updated book of missing persons by the same organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we proceed now with the cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, to what extent did you rely on this book "Ni Krivi Ni Duzni"?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I couldn't quantify that, the number of times I referred to this book. The two main sources for my work were the exhumation documents, the declarations of death; and in the absence of information such as witness statements, testimony, or declarations of death, the use of the book that has been -- using the book that has been mentioned allowed me to obtain an idea of the time when a person went missing in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you do any follow-up or background check, since you have a criminal law enforcement background, to determine what the reliability of that documentation was by the association that produced this book?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Check up. Do you mean interviewing witnesses, or simply do you want to know whether I had access, whether I saw evidence corroborating certain elements?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Including those two that you just mentioned; but also in addition to that, to know what the purpose and goals are of this organisation in producing this book, specifically in setting forth a time line in connection with when persons were missing and when they were allegedly deceased?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As far as the purposes are concerned, the purposes of this organisation, which is an association, well, their objective was to compile a list of people who went missing in the Municipality of Prijedor. For many people, these were family members who were searching for family members who had been -- disappeared. And as far as I know, this work was done in collaboration with the International Commission for Missing People. And it facilitated collection of samples in order to identify bodies exhumed in the Municipality of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this: On page 4 of your report --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, Mr. Sebire: On page 4 of your report, still on the introduction section, sixth paragraph, it states: "The purpose of this report is not to make an assessment on the reliability of the documentation provided to the Office of the Prosecutor." I know you weren't here yesterday, and interestingly enough, we were -- hit an impasse on interpretation of various words including the words "original" and "copy," so I don't want to be presumptuous with any witness and would like to ask you what do you mean that there was no or Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this report does not make an assessment on the reliability of documentation provided by the OTP? My question is actually three-fold: One, what is the documentation you're referring to? Two, do you question the assessment or have you assessed the reliability of any of those documents? And three, why do you not make an assessment as to the reliability of the documents that you utilised, sir, in reaching certain conclusions, preparing certain tables, and giving certain opinions in this testimony, in this trial?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think only the first part of this three-fold question can be answered by the witness. The other two parts are not in the domain of the witness before us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I talk about -- when I refer to -- when I say that the objective of the report wasn't to make an assessment on the reliability of the documentation provided by the Bosnian authorities and the Office of the Prosecutor, well, these are mainly declarations of death by court municipalities. To carry out a complete checkup would imply interviewing or meeting all those who were present when these decisions were made, which means for the 955 cases that we considered in Prijedor, you should take two or three persons to be interviewed and to verify that they made these statements in front of the court in Sanski Most such and such a date. In human terms, this was quite impossible to do, almost impossible to do. On the other hand, these documents were provided in an official manner, and the objective of this report was to use the conclusions, these conclusions. Does that answer your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In part it does, a third of the questions that I asked. In part it does, Mr. Sebire. You mentioned in the introduction paragraphs of your report that there were different rules and procedures that were utilised by the Bosnian authorities, I think as you identify them, respectfully, as well as the OTP. And you also mention that the standards used in exhumations and in identification presumably were different. Can you expand on that for us a little bit and tell us how were they different and why were there two sets of rules and procedures allowed to be implemented in the exhumations of certain gravesites?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: It's possible for various reasons, which are also explained in the introduction, in the same paragraph that you referred to. On the one hand, objectives of the Commission for Missing Persons in Bosnia, which is a social and humanitarian objective, first of all; whereas the objective of the OTP is to gather evidence which is to be presented in front of a Trial Chamber. The other reason is that the means that each party had were different in the case of carrying out exhumations. And this explains that the standards used were different.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How so?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: For example, the time passed by the various commissions in the field, in the case of exhumations, very rarely would an archeologist be present to participate in the operations of identifying the bodies, of unearthing the bodies. In the case of the OTP's operations, there would always be an archeologist there, and all the bodies were -- how should I say? Well, the geometrical position in the grave would be determined. This kind of -- these kind of operations were not conducted by the Bosnian authorities. As a result, there were different periods of time spent carrying out exhumations. This is one of the differences that one can observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just spend a little time with that difference, in fact, of the 20 missions that were done to exhume the bodies, 3 were done specifically by the OTP. Correct? Or representatives from the OTP, correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: You're speaking about 20 missions? I'm not sure I've understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Essentially in your report, you break down that there were 20 exhumations that were done or at 20 intervals exhumations were done. It's my understanding from reading your report that 3 were done by the OTP, 2 were done jointly by the OTP and the Bosnian authorities, and the remaining 15 were done exclusively by the Bosnian authorities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, not quite correct. The figures you have mentioned correspond to the number of sites of mass and individual gravesites that could be connected to incidents mentioned in the indictment. This does not refer to the total number of mass or individual gravesites that were exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I understand that. I know from Section 2 of your report that it's your contention, and obviously based on the information available to you, that there were 261 mass and/or individual gravesites. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, help me with this: How many exhumation missions, if you will, did -- you were involved in one. You mentioned you were there for five weeks. How many were the OTP involved in? Perhaps I can --

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Sorry. Please go ahead. I don't know the exact number. But what is sure is that all the exhumations carried out by the OTP, by the Tribunal, by investigators from the OTP -- investigators from the OTP were present at these exhumations. As far as the exhumations are concerned where the OTP carried out forensic investigations, an investigator from the OTP was also present. And as far as the other cases are concerned, unfortunately I can't tell you how many times investigators from the OTP were present for other exhumations which were carried out by the Bosnian authorities alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, I'm almost losing the point of which I'm talking about in this area, and I'm trying patiently to get to it. But if I can just direct your attention to Section 4, page 10 of your report, 4.1.4. And maybe I could from this discussion go on to the question I'm asking, namely the standards used by the Bosnian authorities and the standards used by the OTP in exhuming these gravesites. Specifically by way of example, the one that you mentioned, the archeologist issue. On 4.1.4 what does it mean when you quite: "The OTP forensic team conducted a total of three exhumations within the territory of the Prijedor Municipality." My question to you, sir, is how many exhumations within the territory of the Prijedor Municipality did the OTP forensic team conduct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Three exhumations carried out entirely by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right. And that's the point I'm trying to make. And if -- I"m just trying to help facilitate this so we can go a little quicker. On 4.1.2, if I ask you the same question: How many exhumation about the OTP forensic team and the Bosnian authorities conduct jointly, would the answer not be, sir, as reflected in your or the on page 10 Section 4.1.2 that, in fact, there were two such exhumations that were performed by the OTP forensic team and the Bosnian authorities jointly?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then how many -- I was able to even understand that. I don't speak French. So sorry about that for the interpreters. How many exhumations were performed by the Bosnian authorities without the OTP team being involved? And maybe I could help you by just pointing out the next section of your report, on page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I think the ambiguity in the answers is due to this type of a question. If team means Team 1, you're going to get one answer from Mr. Sebire. If team means forensic team, you're going to get another answer from Mr. Sebire.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I've read his report, Your Honour, quite frankly, and he identifies 20 sites both in the footnote and in the body of his report. Although it's difficult to get an answer as to whether there were 20 or not, it's irrelevant for our purposes. But I was trying to lay a foundation so that we could ask him the issue with respect to different standards utilised by the various teams specifically the archeologists. This goes to the heart of an issue that the OTP asked them; namely, burial, method of burial for religious faith. And those are the types of question we are going to ask him because Mr. Sebire gave an opinion that I would like to at least be given an opportunity to flush out and to determine how credible that may or main be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm really not objecting. I'm trying at least to help because when the question was missions, if Mr. Sebire goes and observes, that's a mission. If other investigator goes and observes while an exhumation is done, that's a mission and that's a team being present. Forensic team is separate, and his answer will be different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, may I ask the witness to comment on this once again interesting discussion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What I'm referring to in the report is when I talk about the participation of the team from the OTP, it's a forensic team, or either teams that go to the exhumation site, which are composed of archeologists, of anthropologists, of screen of crime technicians, of photographers, and of an investigator dealing with the case in point -- also, forensic teams who work in the morgue. These are the teams I refer to in my report. And in such cases, three exhumations were carried out by the OTP alone, and two in which forensic teams intervened when post mortem operations were being carried out. So there were five cases in which we participated in exhumations by the OTP Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And now there -- thank you for that, it really helped -- five that the OTP participated in. How many were there that the OTP did not participate in, the exhumations that were done exclusively by the Bosnian Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. authorities? 15, right?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: 255, if you have a look at page 11, paragraph 4.1.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I've read it. So in total, the Bosnian authorities exclusively participated in 255 such exhumations; the OTP participated either exclusively or in part with the Bosnian authorities in five. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to the standards which is really all I was trying to accomplish here. Would it be fair to conclude, then, that the standards that you mentioned, such as a lack of an archeologist to detect and denote specifically where the bodies were found within a grave, namely, positions whether they are facing Mecca, east, or any items similar to that, that that archeologist was not present, and therefore no such information is available for you to determine whether or not those individuals were buried by family, friends, or neighbours in an appropriate Muslim burial?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Well, the absence of archeologists doesn't influence this field that -- this domain that you have just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, then what other standards or differences are there in the rules and procedures that you've identified on page 4, Section 1, on your introduction which plainly state that there were differences in how the Bosnian authorities went about exhumations, those 255? They were quite different from the way the OTP conducted their five.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: One of the differences is that time passed in the field, the time spent on the exhumation itself which in general terms can be a shorter period of time when these exhumations are performed by the Bosnian authorities. They will spend a shorter time than the OTP. And this is explained by the presence for the OTP of archeologists, of anthropologists, who take samples that are not made when the Bosnian authorities perform exhumations. So the time spent in the field is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So is it more or less reliable if you spend less or more time in the field analysing, exhuming bodies, and conducting a thorough investigation in a gravesite? What do you believe, that the less time you spend is more reliable, or the more time you spend, then it becomes more reliable?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Unfortunately I can't just answer yes or no to your question. Obviously, the more time you spend, the more details that are recorded in a scientific manner, the more you reduce the risk of error, the chances of identifying the bodies are greater. In most cases, where Bosnian authorities performed exhumations in Prijedor, these exhumations, if you look at the numbers, 255 individual or mass gravesites are concerned, in most cases in the report of the investigating judge dealing with the procedure of exhumation, in general, it is indicated that the Bosnian authorities are aware or were informed by witnesses or by people who buried the bodies of the number of the bodies buried and of the identity of the victims who were buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You're not the first witness from Team 1 that was unable to answer affirmatively or negatively to my questions. But be that as it may, sir, would you agree with me that the reports provided by the OTP are far more reliable, the exhumations that were conducted, are far more reliable than those conducted by the Bosnian authorities because different standards, different rules, and different procedures were utilised? Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As far as this point is concerned, yes, I'd have to agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report -- very rarely do I get. Anyway, in your report, sir, spent what seems to be an incredible and enormous time gathering data and information, inputting, analysing various factors on the individuals and bodies that were exhumed. Namely, you identify things such as the sex and gender of the body to the extent possible. You identify the age of the deceased individuals. You even go as far as to identify the cause of death as well as the ethnic background of certain individuals. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: When it is possible to do so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And by your background, training, education, you are a criminal law enforcement investigator. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, not -- well, I worked only in judicial matters, police dealing with judicial matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the various levels of proof in criminal proceedings such as mere possibility, probability, more probable true than not, based upon a reasonable degree of certainty, beyond reasonable doubt? Are you familiar with those standards of proof?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me with your report, which category would you place it in?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't think I'm the one who should make that judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you like me to make it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the question is argumentative and rhetorical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it was only a rhetorical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, I didn't understand that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, going back to this gathering and inputting of information and factors on the individual bodies that were recovered or deceased individuals, do you know, sir, having been involved in this case with Team Number 1 working with the OTP and various individuals whether or not the allegation and the proposition that the OTP is trying to establish, that intellectuals and educated people within the Prijedor Municipality were actually targeted and were a target group for both killings, beatings, and deportation? I'm sure you're familiar with that having worked with Team 1 for a number of years. Can you tell me, sir, why that data or those tables or that information is not anywhere within your report of 53 pages?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: It could have appeared in the report. In light of the time that I spent on the third part of the report, which is an attempt to draw connections between the exhumations, the incidents mentioned in the indictment, and the witnesses who were called to testify before this Trial Chamber, if you remember the elements that I was to take into account, if you don't have a witness who comes specifically to speak about a person who was either a policeman or a judge or a physician, if nobody comes to speak to say that somebody was killed for that reason, it's difficult to make the connection. But if a witness comes and says that he saw that this or that physician or this or that judge killed in Prijedor, and that that person, in fact, was identified in an exhumation or that for that person, I have a declaration of death from a municipal court, that would be mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now -- and I understand that you don't have a law degree. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not trying to misstate or to expand any opinions that you may have. We as the lawyers are -- or at least I believe -- required to quantify certain groups in connection with various allegations that are being proposed by the OTP. Since we do not have that information from you, sir, and that information is not available, would you agree with me based upon a reasonable degree of certainty, based on your report, the information provided by you, analysed with you by your team and clerks that inputted this data that no such evidence exists that indeed intellectuals of a certain ethnic background were targeted for killings?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, sir: Having conducted and utilised various sources in compiling the data that you did in this report, how difficult would it have been do you think, sir, to go to an educational institution and to gather information and data to determine what the educational level was of citizens within Prijedor of a certain ethnic makeup?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The question is not related to the domain our expert is working in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me switch, if I may, to another topic. Just one last question, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to ethnic background, sir, I note on page 5 of your report you reached this conclusion, paragraph 3, first sentence: "In some instances, the ethnicity was determined even though the victims were not identified."

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to me, sir, how is that even remotely possible; and secondly, just because we are running out of time, secondly if you do make that assumption, clarify for me what the assumptions were that you made and what the per cent of margin of error is in making those presumptions or assumptions in connection with concluding that you can determine ethnicity even though the victims were not identified?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In general, this is information that one gets in exhumation reports prepared by the examining magistrate, that is, the Bosnian authorities. As I have already said, sometimes witnesses give information about people in an individual or a mass grave, saying that he knew that person, was a Bosnian Muslim, couldn't give the name, but the body is exhumed and identified. Through the reports which the magistrate drafts referring to these nonidentified bodies, it can be said that they are probably Bosnian Muslims. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we have to make the break now because this is indeed a question we have to go in some more details. And the trial stays adjourned until 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Before we restart with the cross-examination, I'm more than happy to tell you that Madam Ruzic told me in writing that she'll be able to provide Dutch/English interpretation for tomorrow. So there seems to be no obstacles. So please, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Sebire. I read your answer actually during the break on page 66, and I unfortunately do not understand it, which commences on line 1. However, let me try to approach this a different way, and maybe we could accelerate this process somewhat. It states on page 5 of your report in the section summary of findings in the third paragraph: "In some ins, the ethnicity was determined even though the victims were not identified." There's no question yet, but I'll get to the question right now. From that and in that context, sir, can you tell me since apparently from your report 261 gravesites were found and exhumed, 1394 bodies and body parts were actually exhumed, the number of individuals or the minimum number of individuals as you call it were 1.252. Out of those 1.252 individuals, 581 were identified with certainty as being Bosnian Muslims. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Out of those 581 who are identified with certainty as Bosnian Muslims, how many, sir, how many instances were there that the ethnicity was determined even though the victims were not identified?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: It's 581 individuals who were identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So for all those 581, we know, sir, that in fact 573 of them were Bosnian Muslims. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Basing oneself on the documents that we received, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What else can we base it on other than the documents you received, interpreted, and relied upon?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Well, the major source of identification that I received was the one that I put into our report, that is, it came from the Bosnian authorities who stated that this or that body was taken out of this or that mass grave, and they then identified them. They said at the same time what the ethnicity of the individual was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of the remaining 760 individuals or bodies, you could not with any reasonable degree of certainty identify those corpses, if you will, by way of ethnicity. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you state that your next analysis under proof of death database on page 5, 2.2, that 995 out of this potential 1.252, it can be confirmed, based upon a reasonable degree of certainty, that they died or went missing in the course of the year 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the remainder, if you take the differential between 1.252 and those that with certainty that you can conclude died or went missing, of 955 bodies, what should we conclude with the remainder? That they died before 1992, after 1992?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I think that you're mixing up the figures relating to the people who were deceased and people who were exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me read it on page --

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: 1.255 relates to the minimum number of people who were exhumed. You mention 995 for declarations of death; it's 955, as I said. And the purpose of this report was not to mix the data from the two projects in order to avoid confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right. And I'm not trying to create any confusion. I'm just trying to have a better appreciation for this extensive report that you did. On page 5, the second portion of your summary of findings, 2.2, "Proof of Death Database," you state clearly what I thought I was asking you, that out of the 1.295 court rulings relating to the Municipality of Prijedor declaring individuals as officially dead were received. Sir, then you go on to say: "Out of those, again, 1.295 cases, 955 concern individuals who were killed or went missing in the course of the year 1992." All I'm asking you, based on your report, the analysis that you made, what happened or did you conclude with any certainty when the remainder 300 or so individuals, when they died?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. Among those persons who were not counted in the 955, that is, approximately 300, as you said, there are about 99 cases for whom the decision relating to deceased persons state that that person was killed during combat operations. And in those cases, those people were not included in this presentation. In other cases, they were declared deceased during the year 1993 and 1994, even 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that in your analysis in your report you actually state rather affirmatively that in making a decision or to try to even reconcile whether individuals deceased by virtue of combat or noncombat activities is almost impossible, and that it was one of the most difficult things, if not the most difficult thing, to ascertain?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: When it's done by the Court as regards the deceased persons, I did not include that specific case because it had already been determined that they had been killed during combat -- they had been killed in combat. That's when we would not include them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I understand you, out of the 1.295 court rulings, we have 955 and that you are telling us and have opined and have prepared a report telling us that they died, were killed, or went missing in the course of the year 1992. Correct? And out of the remaining 300 or so, forgive me because I don't have the exact number, out of those remaining 300, is it your position that they died during combat in 1991, 1992, 1993, 1994, and 1995, but you're just uncertain when?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As regards the -- we know the exact year. If you look at page 13, 4.2, for 1992, there were 1.054 decisions declaring people were deceased appear for 1992, and those were received -- those cases were received by the OTP. When one reads the decisions relating to the death of those people, it turned out that 99 of those cases were mentioned as having died during activity -- combat activity. As regards the others, it's true, it's not stated in the report whether these are people who were declared missing or killed outside of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me try it this way, if I may: The 955 concerned individuals who were killed or went missing in the course of the year 1992 versus the 1.295 that you put down as the minimum number of individuals from the exhumation, the difference between that, can you tell us with a reasonable degree of scientific certainty when they died?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection. I don't think the question is comprehensible, given that it's mixing exhumations again with the proof of deaths. If I could expand, or does Your Honour -- the 955 bodies the witness has explained were persons who were both were declarations of both for persons who were listed as having died in 1992 and not having died in combat. The original number in 1992 was 1.054 he said, subtracting the 99 cases, that left 955. He indicated that of the total 1295 declarations of death, 350 subtracting the figures he has -- well, I'm sorry, I don't want to expand on that any further. But the question by the counsel just now concerned the minimum number of people exhumed, which has nothing to do with the 955 figure of individuals who were declared dead in 1992 not in combat by the courts of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this contribution. I think this kind of resolving disputes helps. So please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, I'm really just trying to figure out if we could quantify the number of individuals that you could confirm, based upon a reasonable degree of scientific certainty, actually died in the year of 1992, specifically April through September of 1992. And I know you've provided a table and a chart from that -- for that. However, my question to you, sir, is: From that list, did you, as the OTP's trial counsel contends, did you ultimately from that 800 or 760 that you identified, did you ultimately conclude what percentage died in combat and what percentage died in noncombat activities?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just on the to the leadup to the actual question where counsel indicated that Mr. Sebire was testifying as to the number of people who were killed in 1992. Nowhere in this report does Mr. Sebire make any estimate of the total number of persons killed in Prijedor in 1992. He simply reports those bodies exhumed, and separately those persons declared dead. And he has made very clear that neither of these is likely -- it's not reasonable to believe that either of these is a complete list of those who were killed in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can just briefly respond, as the Court very clearly knows, there are certain allegations proposed by the OTP against our client. The decisional authority in this Tribunal clearly finds that there should be a qualitative and quantitative methodology that should be utilised in ascertaining whether certain threshold issues, specifically those relating to counts 1 and 2 of the fourth revised amended indictment, how is it that we should go about that process, whether we take individuals in a smaller geographic scope, namely, a municipality or a town within a municipality, or do you first examine the total population Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. from the Republic in its entirety. The second fold in that analysis as the Court, I believe, knows and without misstating it permits us to ask questions specifically in order to get and ascertain information so that we can make a reasonable basis as to the percentages of those alleged that may have perished in 1992 and those which, with reasonable degree of certainty and beyond the reasonable doubt, were of Bosnian Muslim ethnic background. For us to establish that, no witness other than this gentleman here, who has prepared an extensive and impressive report, would we be able to conclude with any assurances what those qualitative and quantitative numbers would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I think I can be of a little help to counsel and the Court on this. I'm not sure I agree that we are required to quantify the total number killed, but I will say that we are attempting to do that. That will be part of Ms. Tabeau's coming attraction, her report, which we hope will be available on Monday. And in fact, Ms. Tabeau, and Your Honours, the Defence already has, and I'm not sure if the Court does, her preliminary report that was conducted and that was written to the Keraterm case, which I think Mr. Ostojic was on, in which she does make those figures. That's simply being updated. In that report, what she is going to rely on is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. I think we shouldn't take this in advance, and we should expect this report. Indeed, the cross-examination is intended to contest that what has been said during the examination-in-chief, and the other parts of the expertise. But it would be indeed helpful if the Defence, for example, could base their questions on figures indeed given in this expertise, especially Exhibit Number 281-3, the numbers of declaration of deaths, not included, nonexhumed persons we have before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, is it correct what the Office of the Prosecutor in essence said, that you're not here to give us an opinion and you do not have an opinion with any degree of certainty as to the number of individuals that died in 1992, specifically April through September 1992? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I just indicated that I was not really impressed by the idea to anticipate the expert statement of another expert. So please, refrain from this rather unhelpful expertise, upcoming expertise, and base your questions on the expertise we have before us. No speculations on another expert, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sebire, tell me so that I'm clear and so that I understand, what is your expertise?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: First of all, I'm not an expert. I'm an investigator, and as such, the only work I have to do is to carry out investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. With respect to this report, sir, you've just in essence done, and I apologise for having to paraphrase it, but as I see it what you've done is just taken from two sources, one, the individual investigative aspect, i.e., the exhumations that you performed not only on behalf of the OTP, not only on behalf of the OTP and the Bosnian authorities, but also on behalf of the Bosnian authorities, correct, those 261 gravesites that we discussed. Correct? And what you did, sir, in your analysis was you compared it and made an analysis relying upon, as your report so indicates, relying upon the Bosnian officials, namely and specifically the Court documents which certify or have what you call "proof of death" certificates. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, help me with this: On page 11 of your report, I know you want to go to page 13, but we'll start with page 11 for now. On 4.1.1, you discuss a summary of forensic findings, do you not? 4.4.4 -- strike that. 4.1.4. Do you see that section, sir?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, and within that section, you were asked, and basically were looking at considering four aspects. Correct? Can I have them indented? There's a slash marked before each of the four.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Out of those four, the main difficulties that you had and the most difficulties in assessing or making any degree of certainty included two, right, out of those four? Two -- it was very difficult for you to reach any conclusions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Out of the four points that we attempted to -- how should I put it, to concentrate on, there are aspects which at times were difficult -- it was difficult to obtain information for certain aspects at times.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it not that the main difficulties you experienced out of those four, and you isolated right below that were two, namely, one, cause of death, that was difficult for you to make a determination based upon a reasonable degree of certainty. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I would like to point out that the cause of death, I obtained this on the basis of the post mortem report established by forensic scientists. So from this point of view, all I can do is refer to a document that has been compiled by an expert in that field.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why don't we do it a simpler way. Why don't we look at your report and you tell me Mr. Ostojic cause of death wasn't that difficult. The two difficult ones were time of death, not cause of death, right? Time of death was a problem for you, and it was complicated, as well as determining the "status" of the individuals exhumed. Correct? Those were the two aspects you had trouble with. Right?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In fact, as you have pointed out, we have to deal with the status and the time and the place where the person deceased, and this is part of what we tried to establish. In order to do this, we made use of quite a lot of documents. I don't want to refer to all the documents that were used, but that is one of the points that we had to work on, more than on others, because the cause of death being established by forensic scientists, all we could do was refer to the documents. We could not invent a cause of death. Only forensic scientists could do this. So everything that had to do with the work of investigators, given the documents that were at our disposal, well, this is what allowed us to concentrate on the ethnic origin of the person, the cause of death -- I apologise, the status of the person, and then to concentrate on the moment and the place where the person was seen for the last time or killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So going back to what I was trying to previously ascertain, out of the 955 cases that you can, with a reasonable degree of certainty, tell us perished in the year 1992, because you had some difficulty with it, is there a margin of error plus or minus 1 or 2 - however many individuals you would like - where it was difficult to determine the time of death?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I'm sorry to have to mention this again, but when you mention the figure of 955, once more, we're referring to people who were declared dead by courts in this particular case. We only used the contents of the Court decisions. And in this case, out of the 955 mentioned in the report, as far as I know none of the persons were deceased -- none of those who have been said to be deceased have been found alive to this day. I don't know if you want to refer to the number of people who were declared deceased or to the number of people who were exhumed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me see if I understand this correctly, in this case of persons declared dead, you relied that -- on the fact that the court fixed the date of death, for example, August 1992. And then you put it into your report, and this is shown, then, in the table 281-3. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the table that you have in front of you, that the 955 people who were declared dead by the courts, either by courts in Kljuc or in Sanski Most, witnesses who have appeared before you sometimes would mention some of the victims for whom we had declarations of death. These witness statements did not contradict the contents of the Court decisions, according to which these persons were declared dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So there, indeed, opposed to other forensic problems when you find indeed a grave and a corpse, and you have to fix the date of the death; here it was to a certain extent no problem for you because first of all, you could rely, and you relied -- put it this way: You relied on the date fixed by court. And in addition, you crosschecked whether or not this was in line with testimony given in court or via 92 bis statements. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in fact, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just follow up on the line by the Honourable Court in connection with that. If I may just follow up on the question the Court asked you. Did you, sir, read the witness statements from the witnesses that were informed by you testified in this court, or did you actually read the transcript of their actual testimony, both direct and cross-examination, when you did this crosschecking?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, not the transcripts of the examination, the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you be surprised if I told you that some of the witnesses that you list as purportedly having testified either live in this courtroom or pursuant to 92 bis actually did not testify in either manner such as Witness P33, identified in the transcript -- in the report on page 15; page 16, Witness P30; on page 17, Witness P33; Witness, on page 25, P23; as well as one that I specifically recall that was withdrawn as a witness, both viva voce and pursuant to 92 bis, early in the beginning of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. this trial. And I know his name, I just don't want to reveal it. I'm trying to find the notation for it. And your response is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the question because whether or not Mr. Sebire would be surprised by that is not really an issue for his testimony. I think just to correct counsel, Witness 33 is listed to testify next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just interrupt, Your Honour, if you look at Witness Number 8 that they identified, it was clearly a witness that they withdrew from testifying and did not submit a 92 bis report for that witness. Again, if this witness before us today is saying that he knows they all testified, I want to know what the basis of that testimony is. It's not a major point of our cross. I would like to move on in the limited time that I have to other areas to try to better understand the report. But it's just not accurate, quite frankly, and I'm sure the OTP after reviewing what our objections are cannot confirm that all those individuals that are listed on Mr. Sebire's report did testify either live or pursuant to 92 bis. But I'd like to move on if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, but indeed, we can't move on without thinking about this issue because, indeed, to be cautious, I must say it's to a certain extent misleading because until now, I myself had the impression that - and this can only be the base - this crosscheck was done by or with the assistance of transcripts of the examination-in-chief, cross-examination, and answers to questions by the Judges. Because this could be the only helpful assistance for the Court because what -- qui non est ti non, qui non est ti nondo [phoen], what is not in the file is not in the world. And therefore, I would ask indeed the witness to crosscheck once again this expertise and this documentation on the basis of the names of persons named as victims, missing persons in the transcripts of our case. All other figures are totally misleading, especially for the purpose of an upcoming judgement. Would you be able to provide this to the Court, say, within a fortnight?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just for the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can I first hear the answer of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would involve reading all the transcripts. First of all, when I worked on this report, I worked on the basis of a list of witnesses, and the main source of information that I had. These were signed interviews produced by these witnesses in the past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt that the OTP in general has a list of these names mentioned until now in court or via 92 bis available, and therefore I think it should be no problem at all to bring these names together and ask the witness to crosscheck whether or not this fits in that what he examined on the basis of the Court ruling in the Former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we do have that list of specific individuals' names. I can check. There's a possibility that someone has been compiling those names, but I would mention that very rarely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Shall we give the list to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sure. It would be of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please, the burden of proof is with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: There are 7.000 pages of the transcript to date. And I would just mention, Your Honour knows, that many of the examinations when we talked about people killed, for example, Room 3 massacre, we very rarely asked witnesses to name those that they knew were in the room who were killed. And that it would be a limitation, as opposed to the witness statements which go into more detail about names of individuals. I understand Your Honours' concern. I'll see if we have that, and I should be able to get back to you very shortly on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. But still, it remains the request of the Bench that we ask the OTP to provide a crosscheck of those names available in the transcripts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For purposes of cleanup, if you will, Your Honour, I found on page 41 of the report the two individuals, Witness P21 and P8 which are identified which in our view have not testified in either the live fashion or through 92 bis. Just to that the record is clear, because I was unable to find that cite earlier. In any event, may I proceed, Your Honour. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, still I'm on page 11 of your report and trying to have a better understanding, and with respect to the status of the individuals that we were just discussing before we kind of went off on a little bit of a discussion, the status of the individuals is not the status to determine their ethnicity, but in fact as your report indicates, the status of those individuals is to determine whether or not they were combat or noncombat individuals. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the information that we had. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, the information that you had, I think you clarified for us, was the Court proof of death certificates, but also the witness statements that you've reviewed. Did you, sir, from reviewing any of the information that you have make a determination in addition to the determination made by the court as to the status of those individuals who would be considered combatants or noncombatants?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In certain cases, when we based ourselves on witness statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the difference in number that you found from what the court identified individuals as being combatants and those that you found as being combatants?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: We're talking about declarations of death established by courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right, let me try it this way: One of the sources that you used in reaching some of the conclusions or information provided to us within your report are the court records, proof of death certificates. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the other source that you used was the actual exhumations that we discussed earlier today. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, it's your testimony, if I'm correct - and please correct me if I'm not - is that from the proof of death certificates from the court officials, you were able to determine and find a certain number of individuals who were so-called combatants. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And that number, again, just refresh my recollection, is what?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, did you, from the witness statements or from the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 99. Correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From the 99 that you were able to confirm, were you, other than those 99, were you able to determine what the status of those individuals that were exhumed or considered dead or missing in 1992, were you able to determine their status as being combatants or noncombatants?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: When we had testimony, according to which it was possible to establish this fact, as far as I can remember with regard to this report, and taking into consideration the fact that the exhumations -- taking into consideration the exhumations, I don't remember exhumations in which there were bodies that were identified and these were bodies were identified as being those of combatants.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's of the five exhumations that you did, but not the 255 that the Bosnian authorities did. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: That concerns all the persons identified. The entire figure, 581 -- I'll just check the number. As I said, there were 581 persons who were identified in the exhumations. To date, I haven't discovered elements indicating that these people were combatants. And naturally, these persons weren't just exhumed in the five exhumations which were performed by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of those 581 individuals that you were able with certainty to identify, 573 was confirmed were Bosnian Muslims. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What percentage of a whole of that 573, out of the number that you gave us, 581, was there an assumption made that the ethnicity of the corpse was a Bosnian Muslim?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In this particular case, since we're talking about bodies that were identified, we have identification from authorities who identified these bodies. And we know the ethnic membership of these people. Out of the 581, I would say that in 73 cases -- 573 cases, persons were identified as Muslims, Bosniaks. I didn't receive any elements that contradicted this information provided by the Bosnian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that, Mr. Sebire. In fact, it is only this number that we can actually say with honesty and integrity that can be based upon a reasonable degree of certainty that there is little, if any, doubt as to only those 573 individuals both being identified and being of Muslim ethnic background who were killed or even last seen missing in 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, in fact that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's the number I want to try to use, just to try to shorten this up a little bit. Out of that 573 Bosnian Muslims that were Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. identified based upon a reasonable degree of certainty from the Prijedor Municipality, did you go back, sir, to determine whether any of these were combatants or noncombatants by running through either the Microsoft Access data search programme that you utilised in your report and compare it to either reports used by team members in your team by inputting the names of over approximately 5.000 individuals who were listed as being members of the Territorial Defence of Kozarac, for example, to name one town within that municipality?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: In most cases, checkups were made. It's possible that in individual cases -- that for individual cases, I didn't find all the documents. That is quite possible. As far as belonging to units -- Kozarac units, in certain cases, victims were mentioned as being members of the TO, of the Territorial Defence. But there are no elements that show whether or not the person was killed in combat. Very often, for example, in declarations of death, members of the Territorial Defence from such and such a village would be mentioned. And they would be mentioned as being members of this defence organisation. They would also mention that these persons were arrested and taken to camps. So as I said at the beginning, only when there was certainty with regard to the fact that the person in question was killed in combat, only in such cases would that person be excluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All I want to know is: Did you actually run the data search bases and compare by inputting the names of the individuals from a list that we've identified as being the members of the Kozarac Territorial Defence, and compare it to the 573 individuals in order to reach a conclusion as to what the status of those individuals were, combatant or noncombatant? Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The exercise was done for all those who were declared dead. The database was incorporated into the database for those exhumed, and each time a person was declared deceased, we found the body of the person deceased, it was indicated. And as I said, as soon as there was a declaration of death and information that we had indicated that a person was a combatant, in such cases, this person was systematically excluded from the numbers. So the numbers I have mentioned in the report are for people for whom checkups were made. It's possible, and I can't guarantee this absolutely, it's possible that perhaps I didn't have a document for one or two cases. I don't know. But that's possible. But as far as investigations are concerned, they were done.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Point out to me where in your report that analysis was done and the results of that analysis. What table should I be looking at to find that out?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: First of all, you have to consider the part of the report which has to do with the declarations of death where it is indicated that all of the cases that fall under the category of deceased as part of military activity were not included. The bodies identified were compared with the data in the proof of death; and if the declaration of state said they were killed in combat, then they were not mentioned. There's no specific paragraph that deals with that subject in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Back to page 11 and the status of those exhumed at the time of their death, you state: "The intent was to try to determine whether the individuals exhumed were combatants or noncombatants." The topic that we have been discussing. The result of your attempts or intentions, what were the results, sir? Were they successful, were they a failure, or were they incomplete?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I believe that the results that we obtained are complete. If we take into account the limits of the documents that we used in order to produce this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So were they successful or were they a failure? Because the only item that I see that you utilised in order to make a determination of the status of those individuals was that that was provided to you by the Bosnian officials, namely, the proof of death certificates, the 99 or so that you've previously referenced. But I'm interested to know what your intentions as listed on page 11 of your report, the success of your intentions and your attempts to reach or make such conclusions.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The -- those declarations are not the only source that we used. We also made use of testimony in order to try to limit the -- this report to those witnesses that were chosen for this case. When those witnesses speak about victims, usually I did not try to contradict a witness who said that such and such person died in camp and for whom the body was found and identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I couldn't imagine that you would question a person who's going to identify an individual as being a combatant. But did you do any verification to determine those whose identification as to their status of being a combatant or noncombatant was accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As regards whether a person was a combatant or not, I would have to say that I did base myself on the witness statements and the other documents that I had available to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And those documents are all those that you cite in your report. Correct? Everything you relied on in order to reach the conclusions that you did, everything that you used in order to analyse and incorporate within your report, that's listed expressly and specifically on these 53 pages somewhere. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes. I prepared a list of all the documents, the main documents, that we based ourselves on. Yes, that's correct. And clearly, in light of the quantity of documents and the people who were involved or concerned by this report, it would have been difficult in any case to proceed on a case by case basis and to question three or four people about -- saying that people were either declared missing or were dead in order to establish that they were combatants or not. I think that would be something quite difficult to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For example, nowhere in your report do you mention the exhibit that has been admitted into evidence of the Kozarac Territorial Defence, although it's your contention is that's not a main document or something that you would have expressly stated in your report. It's something that you nonetheless considered and incorporated in reaching your conclusions. Is that what you're telling me?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't really understand that question. I can tell you -- I'm a little bit confused with what it is you're trying to get at.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to give you or try to understand your answer a little thoroughly. Quite frankly it's my understanding from your answer when I asked you if all the documents that you relied upon and reviewed in reaching your conclusions are identified expressly within your report, at which time I recall that you said the "main documents" are listed. Therefore, in trying to be rather clear and thorough, it's fair to state that you did review the Territorial Defence documents of Kozara, but you just didn't list that item as being a main document that you reviewed or considered within your 53-page report. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
