utterances.text: The documents of the Territorial Defence at Kozarac, as regards my report, the document was not used unless it has a different name. If you could tell me what document it is that you're referring to, that would help me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's the only reference that I have for the time being. But that's okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's not okay. Could the Defence please be so kind and present the document you want to mention here to the witness, whether or not it was included. And of course, it's not for the witness to make any conclusions on the status of these persons, but it's only the question whether or not the person mentioned in this document were taken into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's all I'm trying to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. So please, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: D11, if the usher would be kind enough to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If it would cut things short, if Your Honour would accept that, I stipulate that he did not consider that document which is a Defence document not in the OTP computer system that apparently was submitted in the Tadic appeal. He would not have had that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the testimony is of the witness quite frankly. I'm confused as to initially his responses. But be that as it may, I would like in the short time at least -- we can show him the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you have an opportunity to review Exhibit D11?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Briefly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Ever so briefly having reviewed it, do you know, sir, as you sit here whether or not you utilised any of the information contained within D11 when making a determination or assessment as to the status of the individuals that were exhumed and identified as being combatants or noncombatants?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you think, sir, as a reasonable person, that information might have at the very least assisted you in determining whether or not individuals were combatants or noncombatants in order to fulfill specifically the requirement and the complaint that you had with the difficulty of determining what the status of those individuals were?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me turn ever so quickly to another section in your report, and that's Section 5, sir, where you make this linkage between the exhumations, the proof of death, and the crimes committed in the Municipality of Prijedor. Ready? In making that analysis, sir, I note that in some sections you identify specifically a brief summary of the incidents that may have occurred. In other sections when you identify the crimes that were perpetrated, you do not list a brief summary of the incident. Just to speed things up, I direct your attention to the very first 5.1.1 of that section which appears on page 15, and then if you turn to page 26, 5.1.8 which expressly identifies "brief summary of incidents." Take a look at those two. Let me know when you've completed your brief review of it, and then I have a couple questions on that. How is it in some sections you have the brief summary of the incident, and in some you don't? What's the rationale for that? I'm just trying to understand your report.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: There's an important difference between the incident mentioned in 5.1.1 and 5.1.8. In 5.1.1, the title speaks of the killing of a certain number of people in Kozarac and in the surrounding areas in May and June 1992. Among the witnesses to whom I referred to speak about that incident, they don't all speak about the same murder in the same location. As regards the next incident, that is, 5.1.8, there were witnesses who speak about a very specific incident, and a single one, and for which there was an exhumation which completely fits in with that what had been said in respect of that incident, which was a single one. Now in Kozarac, we're talking about many incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So I understand it, is it the reason and -- strike that. You put brief summary of incident when it's limited to a certain time and a certain place because there's more clarity for you, whereas the other instances, it would have been too wide an issue to fully summarise and put down in your report essentially. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The reason why there is no summary for each incident mentioned by the witnesses is that they are included in the general heading of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For example, on page 29, 5.2, when you discuss the killings of a number of men in Room 3 at Keraterm camp on or about the 24th of July, 1992, with respect to that incident, there's no brief summary of the incident. Correct?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: That's right, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to understand your report. And the reason there is in some and not in the other is why?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: It was a question of, well -- how shall I put it? To go back to 5.1.1, for instance, as I've already said, the witnesses speak about an incident that happened in Kozarac and the surrounding area. And one is not going to prepare a summary for each of these witnesses on whom I based myself. I considered that it was simpler to leave those incidents within a general context of the information given.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you able, in conducting your analysis or preparing these tables that you did for us here, for the OTP, these 53 pages, were you able at any time, sir, from reviewing the witnesses' statements and from reading the documents that are on -- as I think on my learned friend said within the OTP database, those documents that are within your control and hopefully within your reach, were you able to figure out, out of each specific instances of killings or death, whether they were done by the police or the military? Did you do that research or analysis?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you ever able to, or did you make an analysis from all the materials available to the OTP and to yourself being a member of Team Number 1, and did you ever prepare a table to determine out of these deaths that you've recited for us in this report how many were done exclusively by third parties from an individual criminal intent; namely, revenge, retaliation, or items similar to that?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No. The object of the report -- the object of the report was not to identify or to name the people directly responsible for the murders which were committed. The objective was to attempt, using the basis, when there was a connection between the exhumations and the incidents mentioned in the indictment, the idea was to indicate that for the victims mentioned by the witnesses, that there were exhumations which allowed identification of the bodies mentioned by the witnesses, or at least that some of the witnesses mentioned by -- the victims mentioned by the witness were dead. The objective of the report was not to identify or to name the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, you can't and don't have any information in connection with the identity of those perpetrators. Correct? Because you have not done that analysis. Right?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: As I said, that was not the intention of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So like, for example, if I look again back on 5.2, specifically 5.2.1, out of the witnesses that -- or the statements that you reviewed from those witnesses, nowhere in that report would there be any relevant data that may be found -- that there were drunken soldiers who invaded the camp on the evening of July 24th, 1991, and in a wild rampage decided unfortunately and tragically to execute individuals within Room Number 3. Nowhere in your report does it say that, does it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's for the Chamber to determine these issues, not for the witness. We heard what is the issue and what was the task for the witness. And no doubt, it was limited to the areas, and not including those mentioned in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may be permitted just one more question on that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Sebire, did you review a signed document by Madam Prosecutor herself which confirms unequivocally and undoubtedly that in connection with the Room 3 massacre, there were "drunken soldiers"? Did you review that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained. Unfair. And I must say that the Defence should take care, as the ruling, not to address this issue any longer -- they should follow this ruling please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct you in the brief time that we have to page 40 of your report if I may. And we are under the witness identified as P50 under the subheading 5.2.2. Are you there? Help me with this, sir. You identify one individual as being a member of the SDA. To what extent does your analysis and preparations of this report conclude whether or not other members that you've identified as being deceased or exhumed or killed or missing within the period of 1992 were members of the SDA or not?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Up to now, it's the only time it is mentioned. The only time I had this information. This morning, I said as regards the exhumation of that person, it was one that was performed by the Bosnian authorities. And unfortunately right now we do not have the entire documentation relating to that exhumation. So I can refer only, when I put that, it's something that -- and I said it this morning as well, this comes from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During the direct examination by my learned friend, Mr. Koumjian, this morning, you stated that there may have been some assumptions made with respect to a differential between the number of individuals identified in the proof of death certificates by the Bosnian officials and those individuals who have been exhumed during the exhumation process, the 261 gravesites that you've mentioned. And I think, if I may paraphrase, one, you said, the assumption was that the family may not have been interested in going to court or the official courthouse to fill out and complete a death certificate. And, two, I think Mr. Koumjian said, the rationale may have been in the discrepancy in the numbers, that there may have been no family survivors. Do you remember that general testimony?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: The point was indicated that the declarations of death were rendered by -- were produced by the municipal courts, and they concerned only individuals for whom the steps were taken by the families. The reason the other families didn't take steps is an assumption. And among one of the possible explanations, it's possible that people who weren't interested in obtaining such a declaration, there were such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar, sir, with the law in Bosnia that requires individuals and families expressly to identify and to fill out forms so that they can have an accurate count once a family member or known person is dead or missing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, objection. The witness is not a lawyer and certainly not an expert in the law of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this question is not only related to law, but more or less to facts, and the factual basis of his own work. Therefore, dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When you say that there's assumptions and you may --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Pardon me, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I dismissed the objection. We are still looking for the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Here I am being presumptuous, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Witness, the Court would like you to answer that last question. I just asked if you were familiar or not, if you had a law degree, but if you're familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: No, I'm not an expert. I'm not a legal expert for Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll take that that you're not a legal expert for Bosnia. But did you ever review or consider the fact that there may be a requirement in that region of persons to identify their next of kin who are either missing or have perished during the years of 1991 through 1995?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I must admit that I don't know whether it's an obligation. I can't answer that question unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: To help the Trial Chamber, I think it would be fair if the Defence could give me a citation to the law in question. I'm not an expert, but that's not my understanding of the law on Bosnia, but I have spoken to some lawyers from Bosnia regarding that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour, or should I respond? I don't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, just so that I can get a concrete figure, do you know if any of the bodies that were exhumed during the 261 exhumations that were performed, whether any of those individuals were from the Prijedor Municipality who were involved in some fashion with the war in either Slovenia or Croatia?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this: Maybe we can narrow it down. Of the 261 gravesites that were exhumed, how many were mass graves and how many were individual graves? Surely you've done that analysis.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I don't have the figures on me unfortunately. In most of the cases, they were individual gravesites or graves containing less than five bodies. Of the 261, unfortunately, I can't give you an exact number. I can't say that there were such and such a number of bodies in one grave. It's quite easy to do. I could inform you of the number, but at the moment I'm not in a position to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That would be very nice of you. I accept. But the way I tried to do the analysis is I took 261 gravesites, and then from that I subtracted the three that the OTP did themselves, which would then leave us with 358. And then I tried to do an analysis from the bodies that you've identified as persons of Bosnian Muslim ethnic background -- actually, when you subtract 261 from 3, you get 258. I think I misspoke and said 358. If you take that analysis, say, from the 3 that the OTP itself has exhumed, you indicate your total is 193 individuals, correct? Page 10 of your report.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, 193 body parts, and 188 bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Actually, I think your report is 193 individuals, and 99 body parts, is it not, for the three sites that the OTP on their own conducted exhumations on? We covered it a little bit this morning. Page 10, first table, 4.1.1.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I take this figure, 191 individuals, how can I determine which individuals -- if I take that number, do I subtract it from the number of 573 Muslims, Bosnian Muslims, that were exhumed and that were individually identified, or do I place that number within the number of 996 that you contend in your report died in 1992?

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: I haven't said that the 193 bodies exhumed by the OTP were all identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me --

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: We must not confuse the figures that correspond to the exhumations in general, the number of bodies exhumed by the OTP or the Bosnian authorities. Based on the general results obtained by these two organisations, the number of bodies that were identified in my report, it's true that I never say that the number of bodies exhumed by the OTP and that were identified and the number of bodies exhumed by the Bosnian authorities who were also identified. I didn't make this difference. I presented it all at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. And also, so we can't really take the number 996, or at one point in your report you identify it as the number 995, individuals that you could with a reasonable degree of certainty confirm died in 1992, we can't take that figure and try to make an analysis based on the three exhumations that you did as listed on page 10 of your report? In addition, we would not be able to utilise the numbers from the two exhumations done by the OTP and the Bosnian authorities. Correct? Can't put the two together.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Once again, you mention the figure 997, I think you mean --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: 996, 995. Oh, the witness.

utterances.speaker: NICOLAS SEBIRE
utterances.text: Excuse me. The number of 996 refers to exhumations. That corresponds to the number of persons for whom we have reason to think that they were deceased in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just a couple more questions, Your Honour, just two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't think that we will come through the testimony of Mr. Sebire today because there are a number of questions remaining. My suggestion is to postpone the end of the cross-examination and additional questions by the Judges to a later day to be determined by the OTP. We would ask the witness, you have given us numerous annexes to your report, to provide us also with a list of persons mentioned by witnesses -- by witness statements admitted under 92 bis or otherwise admitted into evidence as being dead, declared dead, exhumed, missing, and so on, have this list. And then to add, on the basis of your already done expertise, whether or not these persons are to be found on a list of missing persons, whether or not they are declared dead, or whether or not, in fact, they were exhumed. This would be of additional -- of main importance for the Court. And in addition - probably I missed it somewhere - you provided us with a number of annexes, but they don't have any headlines. And one really doesn't know what it means that we have some list of names. Probably you can just provide us with a list of annexes and telling us what is the content of these annexes exactly. So therefore, that it can be, for example, a possibility for this Chamber to find out, just to give you a very simple example on a prominent person, Mr. Muhamed Cehajic, there were witnesses saying this person is dead. And then We know that there is still some hope of the widow, Minka Cehajic, having testified before this Chamber, that is, that the husband is still alive. That we, on the basis of your list, can identify whether Muhamed Cehajic was, indeed, declared dead, found exhumed, or is on a list of missing persons. Just this one example from a prominent person we had in our case until now. As mentioned, there should follow a number of questions emanating from your expertise. And therefore, we want to leave it for the OTP to find a next date for additional hearing of Mr. Sebire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thursday would be an excellent time because apparently I just received -- was passed a note indicating that the witness that was scheduled to testify Thursday, her flight -- the witness's flight was cancelled and will be arriving a day later. So at least if we could start Mr. Sebire on Thursday. I don't know if the witness -- the witness will be here late on I believe Wednesday, so I don't know if it's possible for that witness to testify later on Thursday. But cannot testify Thursday morning. I would ask the Court if the Court personnel have a record of individuals. We do not have a complete record of the individuals named in the testimony as deceased. There are 7.000 pages of transcript. Mr. Sebire, I believe, has already reviewed the 92 bis statements, although he may have been given some -- we'll double check the information he gave-- he was given as to the witnesses that are on the 92 bis list. It may have been out of date. It may have changed since he got the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's try to bring the legal officers together and find a way of assisting you without opening our treasuries. I think this should be feasible, and let's rethink this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so that the Court is aware, I'm unable to proceed with the cross-examination of Mr. Sebire on Thursday or Friday of this week. I'm compelled to testify back home in another matter. So I will not be here Thursday or Friday. So I would ask, if at all convenient, that we try to schedule him any time next week. And with my apologies, again, I thought we would conclude with Mr. Sebire today, and tomorrow's witness as well. But I have to inform the Court, it's just an impossibility for me to be present this Thursday and Friday in this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be feasible and agreeable that we continue the line of questions by the Judges and receive, in the meantime, the additional - if possible, additional report - and then later on we come back to Mr. Sebire for your final questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. I may not have any questions after the Court questions the witness. So yes, that would be agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Apparently Ms. Sutherland believes that she can be ready with the witness on Thursday, can speak to the witness late on Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So we leave it to the OTP to schedule this date in the light of Mr. Ostojic's mandatory absence. But if not, let us please -- if the witness is not available Thursday in the morning, please, let's start with Mr. Sebire, if it's possible for you, at 9.30 on Thursday. Priority is given, no doubt, to the witness if the witness is available. I want to inform the parties and the participants, especially the interpreters, if there are no mandatory objections, my intention is tomorrow to hear the expert on handwriting from 11.00 to 12.30, from 13.00 to 14.00, and from 14.30 to 16.00. This is a little bit exceptional, but caused by the late start. Then finally, because, no doubt, this book may be of some importance and may have some probative value, the document "Ni Krivi Ni Duzni" is admitted into evidence as S282. Any urgent matters?
